title: Agritourism for Kurnool District
subtitle: A practical, farmer-owned model to convert Kurnool’s horticulture, heritage and rural culture into supplementary income.
audience: Immediate opportunity: pilot 8–12 centres around existing tourism and horticulture clusters, then scale by mandal.

sections.title: Market signal: large domestic tourism base, limited farm experience supply
sections.lead: Domestic tourists are the core market; schools, families and weekend travellers are priority segments.

items.desc: Accessible, day-trip friendly, education-led farm visits
Mango, banana, sweet orange, pomegranate, guava; onion & chillies
Urban families seek authentic rural food, open space and hands-on learning
Supplementary income reduces dependence on volatile crop prices and rainfall
Demonstration of natural farming and other agri practices

blocks.label: Core proposition for the district
blocks.text: Convert existing farms into curated learning destinations with low additional capital.

sections.title: Case study anchor: ATDC Baramati, Maharashtra
sections.lead: The model demonstrates how working farms can add tourism income without replacing agriculture.

blocks.label: PILOT LAUNCHED · 2005
blocks.text: ATDC was incorporated with a 38-acre pilot near Pune / Baramati and trained farmers to run agritourism as supplementary income.

items.title: Farmer-owned assets
items.body: Use land, crops, livestock, food and culture already present.

items.title: ATDC support
items.body: Training, project reports, marketing and tour coordination.

items.title: Urban visitors
items.body: Schools, families, corporates and tourists from nearby cities.

items.title: Local income
items.body: Fees, meals, stays, farm produce and employment.

blocks.label: Transferable lesson
blocks.text: ATDC works because it centralises skills and market access, while farmers retain ownership and authenticity.

sections.title: How the ATDC model operates
sections.lead: A hub-and-spoke system: central support + farmer-owned farm experiences.

stages.name: Package visits
stages.desc: Food, farm walk, rides, culture, stays

stages.name: Deliver locally
stages.desc: Farmer, SHGs, youth, artisans host visitors

blocks.label: Institutional spine
blocks.text: Agriculture + Tourism departments / district administration provide registration, convergence, quality checks, school-linkages and risk governance.

sections.title: Reported impact in Maharashtra: demand, income and scale
sections.lead: Use as benchmark, not as guarantee; figures are from the case-study/ATDC survey base.

items.label: Million Tourists (5 lakhs Foreign Tourist)
items.qualifier: As per latest data on website

blocks.label: Policy lever observed in Maharashtra
blocks.text: Annual education visits by Classes V–X helped convert schools into stable weekday demand.

sections.title: Experiences offered: the product is the working farm
sections.lead: The visitor pays for interpretation, participation, food and culture—not only accommodation.

items.title: Farm learning
items.body: Crop walk, seed-to-market story, soil and water practices, natural farming

items.title: Rural recreation
items.body: Bullock-cart/tractor rides, games, safe open-space activities

items.title: Farm-to-plate
items.body: Traditional meals, millet menus, produce tasting, cooking demos

items.title: Local culture
items.body: Folk arts, village festivals, handloom/craft displays

items.title: Direct sales
items.body: Fresh produce, processed foods, seeds, SHG products

items.title: School modules
items.body: Age-wise learning kits linked to agriculture and environment

sections.title: Why the model works for government and farmers
sections.lead: It spreads benefits while keeping capital requirements moderate and assets locally owned.

items.desc: connects dispersed farms to urban demand
FSSAI, toilets, drinking water, waste management
first-aid, liability, animals, water bodies, child groups
crop calendars, festival calendars, school calendar
water use, carrying capacity, no plastics

sections.title: Replication opportunity in Kurnool: cluster, do not scatter
sections.lead: Start where agriculture, tourism anchors and access already overlap.

blocks.text: Minimum standard: 1-acre farm base; 5-acre threshold for school picnics can be adopted from Maharashtra as a safety benchmark.

items.desc: Day trips, airport gateway, adventure + farm visits
Pilgrim add-on packages and traditional food experiences
Mango, sweet orange, pomegranate, onion/chilli stories

sections.title: Decision slide: 90-day pilot launch pathway
sections.lead: A low-risk pilot can demonstrate demand before scale-up investments.

items.title: Constitute District AgriTourism Cell
items.body: Tourism, Agriculture, Horticulture, Education, DRDA/SERB, FPOs, SHGs

items.title: Select 8–12 pilot farms
items.body: Access, safety, horticulture diversity, toilets/water, motivated farmers

items.title: Training + product design
items.body: Hygiene, pricing, farm interpretation, school modules, safety SOP

items.title: Soft launch
items.body: Schools, officials, local influencers, tour operators, feedback capture

items.title: District rollout plan
items.body: Branding, booking page, convergence funds, monitoring dashboard

blocks.label: Immediate ask from District Administration
blocks.text: Approve pilot cell, shortlist farms, nominate nodal officers and permit a joint field visit to Maharashtra/ATDC for operational learning.
